summary.text: Joseph Addabbo Jr. is the Democratic incumbent for New York State Senate District 15, which covers central and southern Queens, and has held the seat since 2009.

A lifelong Queens resident and the son of a former U.S. Representative, he practiced law for about a decade and served seven years on the New York City Council before his 2008 election to the Senate, where he chairs the Committee on Racing, Gaming and Wagering.
He is seeking re-election against Conservative Party candidate Danniel Maio.

paragraphs.text: Addabbo was born in 1964, the youngest child of Joseph and Grace Addabbo; his father, Joseph P. Addabbo Sr., was a U.S. Representative.
He describes himself as a lifelong Queens resident.
He attended Nativity BVM School in Ozone Park and Archbishop Molloy High School, then earned a bachelor's degree from St. John's University in 1986 and a law degree from Touro Law School in 1992.
He practiced law for about ten years, including as an attorney at Addabbo and Greenberg, before entering the City Council.
His official biography also lists former roles as Executive Secretary of Community Board 10Q and president of the Ozone Tudor Civic Association.
Addabbo was elected to the New York City Council in 2001 and served seven years representing the 32nd District, working on infrastructure, school technology and community-services funding.
He was elected to the State Senate in 2008, assumed office in 2009, and won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for re-election over Albert Baldeo.

He chairs the Senate Committees on Racing, Gaming and Wagering and on State-Native American Relations, and is a member of the Budget and Revenue, Cities 1, Education, Insurance, Rules, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.

According to his official biography, Addabbo is a multi-term member of the New York State Democratic Committee, ranking member of the South Queens Regular Democratic Club, a member of Ozone Park Kiwanis and of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force on Hurricane Sandy, and a 2026 New York State Senate Veterans' Hall of Fame Honoree.
He is married to Dawn, and they have two daughters.
